newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds give up ground after solid run.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds give up ground after solid run.

text.p: *Australian bonds gave up some of their recent strong price gains with the market finding itself in something of a void in the absence of any major data over the next couple of weeks.
*Focus on a clutch of U.S. data later on Tuesday.
Australian bonds gave up some of their recent strong price gains with the market finding itself in something of a void in the absence of any major data over the next couple of weeks.

And as the market has more or less priced in a 50 basis points cut in official interest rates, until the Reserve Bank endorses such a move, the market is likely to be dependent on U.S. Treasuries for direction, traders said.
"It's been a phenomenal run, but now the market is in something of a void. Nobody is selling the market aggressively, and I don't expect to see a huge sell-off," said one trader.

Yields hit their lowest level in 3-1/4 years on Monday, dropping a full point in just over a month, amid expectations of a local easing and signs that the Federal Reserve may refrain from a tightening when policy makers meet in early July.
The November 2006 bond yield was holding just below 7.0 percent, while the October 2007 stock, which is increasingly being seen as the benchmark, has crept above that level.

First quarter dwelling commencements are due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), but more importance is being given to the clutch of U.S. data later on Tuesday, comprising CPI, housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation for May.

The mildly negative tone saw spread differentials widen against the dollar bloc. The 10-year spread to the U.S., based on the local November 2006 bond, had briefly narrowed to below 50 basis points to the U.S. for the first time in over a decade on Monday.
